hints.title: Test the conditions separately
hints.body: For each condition, ask whether a parallelogram satisfying it must have both equal sides and right angles. Try varying an angle or a side length while keeping that one condition true.
hints.recap: A sufficient condition must force every requirement for a square.
hints.pitfall: Do not combine two listed conditions when testing one of them.
hints.pause: Draw a possible nonsquare example for each condition and check it.

recall.reminder: A sufficient condition must force every requirement for a square.

hints.title: Use the parallelogram facts
hints.body: Opposite sides are equal and parallel; adjacent angles add to a straight angle. Add the information from each condition to these facts.
hints.recap: A geometry counterexample must satisfy all the given assumptions.
hints.pitfall: Right angles at the vertices and right angles between diagonals are different conditions.
hints.pause: For each case, give a proof or verify a nonsquare example, then select the row.

recall.reminder: A geometry counterexample must satisfy all the given assumptions.

solution:
I is not sufficient: a nonsquare rhombus is a parallelogram with equal adjacent sides.

II is not sufficient either: the same nonsquare rhombus has perpendicular diagonals. For example, a diamond with diagonals of lengths 4 and 2 has equal sides but is not a square.

III forces adjacent angles to be equal and supplementary, hence both 90∘. It therefore forces a rectangle, but a 2-by-1 rectangle satisfies it without being a square.

No condition is individually sufficient: H.
knowledgePattern: Use non-square parallelograms to test separate sufficient conditions
